title: Fix affinity handoff for ephemeral proxy chains with shadowed subprojects
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary: We've observed a class of multi-tenant attribution regressions where requests routed through ephemeral API-key proxy chains are being charged against the parent org/project instead of the intended subproject. This manifests after an upstream credential rotation or when a proxy rewrites claims mid-flight, causing quota drains on the wrong entity and unexpected billing spikes.

Observed impact:
- Incorrect per-project and per-org metering (billing spikes for root orgs).
- Rate limiter counters and quota checks decrement against the wrong tenant, allowing subprojects to exceed their limits while parent projects get charged.
- Several customers (internal and external) reported unexplained quota exhaustion and subsequent request throttles.

How to reproduce (internal staging):
1) Create tenant T1 with subproject S1.
2) Provision an ephemeral delegated API key via integration proxy that injects a proxied Authorization header.
3) Start steady request stream through proxy.
4) Trigger a service-account/key rotation upstream while requests are in flight.
5) Observe token-validation service logs (token-resolver) and the metering pipeline: a subset of requests are attributed to T1 instead of S1; rate-limiter counters show decrements on the parent quota.

Root cause hypothesis:
- The claim resolution path in the ingress/token-resolver uses a cached token->project mapping entry without a strong binding to the ephemeral token nonce. During rotation, the cache entry is evicted then rehydrated; concurrent requests observe a transient mapping state (null/old binding) and fall back to the owning org ID in the downstream attribution step.
- The attribution pipeline reads request headers and internal auth claims in two separate stages; the ordering between publishing the new binding (post-rotate) and the ingress attribution read is not strongly ordered, leading to a race that biased attribution toward the parent org.

Proposed fix:
1) Make claim resolution atomic for ephemeral tokens: include token-nonce in cache keys and ensure resolution publishes the final binding before the request is allowed to proceed.
2) Add an explicit X-Original-Project header at ingress derived from the validated claim (computed once and trusted downstream) so downstream metering and rate limiting consume a single canonical source of truth.
3) Harden the token rotation path to publish binding updates to the attribution service via a write-ahead event and wait-for-ack for the first rotated token batch.
4) Add defensive checks in the attribution pipeline to reject ambiguous mapping (do not fall back automatically to root org when project is unknown; instead mark for reconciliation and route to a safe fallback model).
5) Add unit and integration tests that simulate in-flight rotations and assert no cross-tenant attribution occurs.
6) Add reconciliation job to detect and retroactively re-attribute short windows of misattributed usage for the last 30 days (initial scope limited to customers with confirmed anomalies).

Implementation notes:
- Code changes primarily in ingress/token-resolver (Go) and metering/attribution pipeline (Python).
- New metrics: attribution_decisions{outcome,reason}, ephemeral_token_resolution_latency, attribution_cache_evictions_by_type.
- New logs: correlation_id, token_nonce, resolved_project_id (PII-free).
- Minor schema change for internal request envelope to carry resolved_project_id as a strongly-typed field. Ensure changes are backwards-compatible for older consumers.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for resolver cache key semantics.
- e2e staging test that uses a traffic generator to reproduce rotation race at 500rps and asserts zero misattributions.
- Canary rollout to 5% of hosted region eu-west-1 for 24 hours with monitored alarms.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge feature branch behind a feature flag.
2) Deploy token-resolver + attribution pipeline changes to staging; run extended e2e.
3) Canary to dedicated eu-west-1 hosted fleet (5% traffic) for 24–48h.
4) If stable, ramp to 50% and then 100% over 48h.
5) Run the reconciliation job on the confirmed affected customers within 7 days.

Monitoring, alerts and dashboards:
- Create a dashboard: "Attribution Integrity" with time series for: attribution_decisions[outcome=misattributed], per-project rate-limiter decrement deltas, and reconciliation job progress.
- Alert: misattributed_rate > 0.05% sustained for 5m => P1 paging to on-call.

Notes and links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/KB/attribution-ephemeral-proxy-chains (draft)
- Staging e2e harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1428 (WIP)
- Initial incident ticket: INC-2026-0312 (internal)

Acceptance criteria:
- No misattributions in the staging e2e under simulated rotations.
- Canary shows <0.01% misattribution and no customer-visible quota regressions.
- Reconciliation job correctly updates billing ledger for confirmed customers and provides audit log entries.
